text:
The old beggars say nothing, do nothing.

They know it is useless and exhausting. They let themselves be. They let themselves be.

They let themselves be in sun or rain, with the same air of whole worth,

far from the body they leave anywhere.

They amuse themselves by stretching life through thought.

If someone speaks, his voice flees like a bird that falls.

And it is so unforeseen, unnecessary, and surprising

that to hear it properly perhaps they groan some ah.

Oh, they did not groan, no!… The old beggars are all Stoics.

They will place their misery beside the gardens of the happy world

but do not want those on the other side to know of the strange fate

that runs through them like a river through a country.

The old beggars live outside life: they have excluded themselves.

They open dreams and silences and naked spaces around them.

They have their empty kingdom, of high stars that do not shelter.

Their gaze never looks and their mouth neither calls nor laughs.

And their body neither suffers nor enjoys. And their hand neither takes nor begs.

And their heart is a thing that, if it existed, would suddenly forget.

Ah!, the old beggars are a people turning into stone.

That people, which is mine.

translation.title: Lineage
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of a Portuguese original. The stark repetitions and final identification are retained.
